'''''Lotus dorycnium''''', previously known by the [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]] ''Dorycnium pentaphyllum'',<ref name=POWO_503605-1/> common names: '''prostrate Canary clover''' and '''badassi''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007|accessdate=17 October 2014|df=dmy-all}}</ref> is a [[herbaceous]] [[perennial]] plant belonging to the genus ''[[Lotus (genus)|Lotus]]'' of the family [[Fabaceae]].<ref name=POWO_503605-1/>

==Description==
''Lotus dorycnium'' reaches an average height of {{convert|10|-|70|cm}}. The stems and the branches are woody. The leaves are composed by five segments and are hairy on both sides. Flowers are small and white, in terminal umbels of 5–20 flowers on a short stalk. The flowering period extends from May until July. The fruits are ovoid reddish-brown legumes {{convert|3|-|6|mm}} long containing one or two seeds.

==Distribution==
''Lotus dorycnium'' has a broadly Mediterranean distribution.<ref name=POWO_503605-1/>

==Habitat==
These plants prefer semi-arid hills, sunny and dry pastures and Mediterranean environment and tolerates all soil types.  They can be found at an altitude of {{convert|0|-|1300|m}}.
